business: Hallowsand, a fictional five-bedroom house on a 60-hectare tidal island off the Northumberland coast, let whole by the week from April to October at £3,150–£6,750. The island is reached by a mile of causeway that floods twice a day, and the proposition is the constraint rather than the house: for roughly ten hours of every day nobody can drive on or off. Every crossing window, closure, arrival time, departure deadline and price on the site is computed from a two-constituent harmonic tidal model (M2 and S2) rather than written by hand, and the site says on every page that the island is invented and that nobody should plan a real crossing from it. Its audience is people choosing a week — families, groups of friends, and writers on working retreats — who need to know before paying which hours of which days they will lose.
businessKind: hospitality lettings and places to stay
directionLabel: The tide as the visual material — a computed day ribbon at four densities
businessFacetsNote: Somebody stays; the island is the product and reaching it is a decision; a week costs thousands and is booked once; and what is bought is how the place feels.
